Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=9x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=9 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 9x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =9x\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\cdot 9\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}9x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =3x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3}-3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =3(\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =3(\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot 0-0\cdot 0)+(-1-1) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
